questions.calculus-section-9-6-1: The interaction increases the predator derivative and decreases the prey derivative. The negative x² term in(b) limits prey even without predators.
questions.calculus-section-9-6-2: Inspect the signs of the cross effects. In(a), dy/dt=0.08x+0.00004xy as actually printed; this still increases with x for nonnegative populations. In(b), each species also has a negative quadratic self-limiting term.
questions.calculus-section-9-6-3: For coexistence solve4x+y=500 and2x+y=400, givingx=50,y=300. Axis equilibria describe extinction of one or both species; the interior point has both populations constant.
questions.calculus-section-9-6-4: Use mass-action encounter terms LH and HW. The uncoupled growth signs follow the stated absence assumptions. Other reasonable models are possible; this checks one explicit model.
questions.calculus-section-9-6-5: Follow the printed arrow from the marked point near(300,100) along the lower branch to the right, then upward, leftward and downward. The closed loop indicates repeated states; precise periods are not encoded.
questions.calculus-section-9-6-6: Follow the curve from the marked upper endpoint toward its leftmost point, then its low point, then the rightmost point and inward. The displayed finite curve alone does not specify an exact limiting population or period.
questions.calculus-section-9-6-7: Plot simultaneous population pairs. Initially both rise, then species1 turns down while species2 continues up; the repeating time traces produce a counterclockwise loop.
questions.calculus-section-9-6-8: Read simultaneous values from the two time graphs, not one population against time. Species2 reaches its minimum before species1 reaches its maximum; then both approach their respective limits.
questions.calculus-section-9-6-9: Separate the slope equation for positive populations and integrate. Exponentiating gives the stated invariant; substitute the initial point for its constant. Axis equilibria require separate treatment.
questions.calculus-section-9-6-10: Set both derivatives to zero for equilibria. Nullclines areL=200 andA=5000; their signs give the cycle direction and predator lag. The origin represents joint extinction and the positive equilibrium constant coexistence.
questions.calculus-section-9-6-11: The wolf nullcline givesR=1000; substituting into the rabbit equation givesW=.08(1−.2)/.001=64. The displayed inward spiral approaches this coexistence point.
questions.calculus-section-9-6-12: The positive equilibrium hasA=5000 fromL′=0, thenL=100 fromA′=0. The Jacobian there has trace−1 and determinant.5, giving eigenvalues(−1±i)/2 and a stable spiral. Axis solutions are special and do not approach coexistence.
